q-170378.name: Question 1
q-170378.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170378.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The  maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-138086.name: Question 2
q-138086.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-138086.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1))x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+4x1x2+x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
15[−12]
b
12[−11]
c
120[−25]
d
12[11]
e
13[12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1221]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−1:

A−(−1)I=[1221]+[1001]=[2222] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−1))x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−11].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umin=v‖v‖=12[−11].

q-136827.name: Question 3
q-136827.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $5.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-136827.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−4x1x2+4x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 5. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[−11]
b
15[21]
c
[11]
d
[−12]
e
15[−12]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−2−24]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=5:

A−5I=[1−2−24]−5[1001]=[−4−2−2−1] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−5I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−12].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[−12].

q-170402.name: Question 4
q-170402.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+9{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $0.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170402.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The  maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-0I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-0I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−6x1x2+9x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 0. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
15[21]
b
110[31]
c
110[−13]
d
15[−21]
e
15[−12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−3−39]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=0:

A−0I=[1−3−39]−0[1001]=[1−3−39] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−0I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[31].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umin=v‖v‖=110[31].

q-138085.name: Question 5
q-138085.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $2.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-138085.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

A=[3−1−13]

A−2I=[3−1−13]−2[1001]=[1−1−11] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−2I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[11].

q-170414.name: Question 6
q-170414.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}-17{x}_{2}^{2}+7{x}_{3}^{2}-18{x}_{2}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170414.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-20)I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -17 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 7\end{aligned}]+20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}19 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & -9 & 27\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-20)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−9x22−x32−6x2x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −10. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[011]
b
110[031]
c
15[012]
d
[100]
e
[010]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1000−9−30−3−1]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−10:

A−(−10)I=[1000−9−30−3−1]+10[100010001]=[110001−30−39]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−10)I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[031].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umin=v‖v‖=110[031].

q-170412.name: Question 8
q-170412.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+14{x}_{3}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-170412.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & -19 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−4x12+x22+14x32−24x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[−110]
b
15[012]
c
15[−201]
d
15[−102]
e
12[−101]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−40−12010−12014]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=20:

A−20I=[−40−12010−12014]−20[100010001]=[−240−120−190−120−6]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−20I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−102].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[−102].

q-138090.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-138090.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

So, we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=3x12+x22+3x32−2x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[10−1]
b
[010]
c
13[1−11]
d
12[110]
e
[011]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[30−1010−103]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=1:

A−I=[30−1010−103]−[100010001]=[20−1000−102]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[010].

So, we get

umin=[010].

q-138095.name: Question 10
q-138095.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $3.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-138095.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 10
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−x12+2x22+x32+4x1x2, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 3. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[110]
b
13[111]
c
15[120]
d
15[001]
e
15[20−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−120220001]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=3:

A−3I=[−120220001]−3[100010001]=[−4202−1000−2]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−3I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[120].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[120].

q-170514.name: Question 11
q-170514.problem: The minimum value of $Q(x)=8{x}_{1}^{2}-30{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-50{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $4{x}_{1}^{2}+25{x}_{2}^{2}=100,$ is $-250.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170514.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & -15 \\ -15 & -50\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=5$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=2$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{5}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{2},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & -15 \\ -15 & -50\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 & -75 \\ -30 & -100\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}200 & -150 \\ -150 & -200\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we minimize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the minimum value of the quadratic form is $-250,$ we have

$$
min\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{min}=-250.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-250:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-250I) & =[\begin{aligned}200 & -150 \\ -150 & -200\end{aligned}]+250[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}450 & -150 \\ -150 & 50\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-(-250I))y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{min}} & =P{u}_{\text{min}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-170527.problem: The minimum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-12{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-9{x}_{2}^{2},$ when ${x}_{1}^{2}+9{x}_{2}^{2}=9,$ is $-18.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
q-170527.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=3$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{3}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -6 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -18 \\ -18 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we minimize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the minimum value of the quadratic form is $-18,$ we have

$$
min\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{min}=-18.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-18:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-18)I & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -18 \\ -18 & -9\end{aligned}]+18[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}36 & -18 \\ -18 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-(-18)I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{min}} & =P{u}_{\text{min}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-170138.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=36,$ is $40.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-170138.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=3$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{3},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $40,$ we have

$$
max\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{max}=40.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=40:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-40I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}]-40[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-36 & -12 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-40I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

The maximum value of Q(x)=x12−4x1x2+4x22, when 9x12+4x22=36, is 40. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[−26]
b
110[−13]
c
15[−12]
d
12[−23]
e
110[−29]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−2−24]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2232=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=3 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x23,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[2003],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2003][1−2−24][2003]=[2−4−612][2003]=[4−12−1236].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is 40, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=40.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=40:

B−40I=[4−12−1236]−40[1001]=[−36−12−12−4] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−40I)y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−13]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umax=v‖v‖=110[−13].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmax=Pumax=[2003]⋅110[−13]=110[−29]

q-170560.name: Question 14
q-170560.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)=4{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=36,$ is $25.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
q-170560.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=3$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{3},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $25,$ we have

$$
max\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{max}=25.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=25:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-25I & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}]-25[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 12 \\ 12 & -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-25I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=5,$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The maximum value of Q(x)=4x12+4x1x2+x22, when 9x12+4x22=36, is 25. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[89]
b
12[23]
c
12[−32]
d
15[43]
e
15[12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[4221]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2232=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=3 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x23,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[2003],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2003][4221][2003]=[8463][2003]=[1612129].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is 25, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=25.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=25:

B−25I=[1612129]−25[1001]=[−91212−16] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−25I)y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[43]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[43].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmax=Pumax=[2003]⋅15[43]=15[89]

q-170513.name: Question 15
q-170513.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=3$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{3},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -4 \\ -6 & -12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}36 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following:   

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}36-\lambda  & -12 \\ -12 & 36-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (36-\lambda )(36-\lambda )-144 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-72\lambda +1\,152 & =0 \\ (\lambda -48)(\lambda -24) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =48,\,24\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
min\{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}=24.
$$
